title: OpenStax IA 2e Ex. 9.59: factor a = −3 before completing the square
stem_student: Rewrite f(x) = −3x^2 − 6x − 1 in the form f(x) = a(x − h)^2 + k by completing the square. Factor −3 from the x^2 and x terms first — do not complete the square as if a were 1.
stem_teacher: Named fracture: forgetting to factor a (brief misconception forget-factor-a). OpenStax §9.7 Example 9.59 is the worked a ≠ 1 rewrite. Keep the constant −1 outside the factor.
answer_verification: Copied from OpenStax Intermediate Algebra 2e §9.7 Example 9.59 steps: factor −3 from the x terms; half of 2 is 1; the +1 inside is multiplied by −3 so add 3 outside; rewrite as −3(x + 1)^2 + 2. Author-checked: −3(x^2 + 2x + 1) − 1 + 3 = −3(x + 1)^2 + 2.
attribution: OpenStax Intermediate Algebra 2e, §9.7 Example 9.59 (Lynn Marecek, Andrea Honeycutt Mathis). CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. https://openstax.org/books/intermediate-algebra-2e/pages/1-introduction
provenance_notes: M4-L2 bank fill 2026-09-11. Dedicated a ≠ 1 fracture item. OpenStax warns to factor a from the x terms only, not the constant.
